title: Schizophrenia & Depression: CBT & Psychological Therapies
welcome_lead: Beck's challenges become Aaron's tools for changing minds.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology schizophrenia depression CBT cognitive behavioural therapy effectiveness.
final_note: CBT works by treating thoughts as testable hypotheses.

concepts.def: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy — challenges thoughts and behaviour.
Increasing rewarding activity to lift mood.
Empirical disputation of hallucinations and delusions.
Telling schizophrenic clients others have unusual experiences too.
Ellis's Rational Emotive Behaviour Therapy — extends ABC with D and E.

walkthroughs.body_html: CBT for depression challenges Beck's negative triad. Clients keep thought diaries, identify distortions and test predictions. Behavioural activation tackles withdrawal. NICE recommends 16-20 sessions. March et al. (2007): 81% of adolescents improved with CBT vs 81% with SSRIs — CBT had lower relapse.

Ellis extended his ABC model: D = disputing irrational beliefs, E = effect of new beliefs. Disputing can be empirical (evidence), logical (consistency), or pragmatic (usefulness). Unconditional positive regard supports the work.

CBT for schizophrenia (CBTp) helps clients reality-test delusions and normalise unusual experiences. NICE (2014) recommends at least 16 sessions alongside antipsychotics. Jauhar et al. (2014) meta-analysis found a small effect (d = 0.40) on symptoms.
